sections.name: ParsedDocument
sections.title: Parsed document record
sections.what: Holds the text from one part of a file, such as a page, slide, sheet or message, along with where that part came from. Fields that do not apply to a file type stay blank.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives every parser one record format that the search index can read. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Location fields are optional, so a parser that forgets to fill them produces records with no page or slide number.

sections.name: DocumentChunk
sections.title: Document chunk record
sections.what: Works like a parsed record but for a small piece of text cut from a document. It adds a position number so the pieces can be put back in order.
sections.why: Likely reason: prepared for splitting long text before search. Reason not stated, and nothing in this file creates chunks.
sections.watch_out: Nothing in this file creates chunks, so this record only matters once a splitting step uses it.

sections.name: BaseParser
sections.title: Parser template rules
sections.what: Sets the rules every file parser must follow: one method that reads a file and returns its records, and one that says whether the parser handles that file. It also provides a helper that returns the file ending in lowercase.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the parser manager able to use any parser the same way. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A new parser that leaves out either required method cannot be created at all.

summary: Defines the shared record formats for parsed text and the rules every file parser must follow.
purpose: Gives every file parser one common output format and one common set of methods, so the rest of the app can treat them alike.
why: Likely reason: lets the parser manager use Word, Excel, PDF, PowerPoint and email parsers in the same way. Reason not stated in the code.
how: A parser reads a file and returns a list of parsed records, one per page, slide, sheet or message. Each record holds the text, the file name and type, and optional location fields. Chunk records hold the same kind of data plus a position number for later splitting. Every parser must provide a method that reads a file and a method that says whether it can handle a file. A shared helper returns the lowercase file ending.
inputs: A file path as text, passed to the parsing and checking methods.
outputs: Lists of parsed records from parsing. Chunk records are defined here but nothing in this file creates them.
risks: Any new parser that does not provide both required methods cannot be created at all. Location fields are optional, so a parser that forgets to fill them produces records with no page or slide number.
debug: If a parser cannot be created, look for a missing required method in that parser. If page or slide numbers are blank, check how the specific parser fills them.
